summary: CCC-built 120-foot wood tower in Green Swamp, erected October 1938 from Camp P-73; staffing ended November 2005. No source found on its condition today.

facts.design: 120-foot creosoted wood tower with an inside stairway
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erected by the CCC from Camp P-73 on October 11, 1938.
Camp P-73 completed a 30 by 36 foot, four-room frame house at the tower in January 1939.

evidence.supports: 120-foot creosoted wood tower with inside stairway, in Green Swamp, Brunswick County
evidence.quote: 120 foot creosoted wood tower, inside stairway, located in Green Swamp, Brunswick County

evidence.supports: The report is the 1940 Department of Conservation and Development 8th Biennial Report
evidence.quote: Department of Conservation and Development - 8th Biennial Report - 1940

evidence.supports: Four-room frame house at the tower, 30 by 36 feet, completed January 1939 by Camp P-73; entry spells the name Riegal
evidence.quote: 30' x 36' 4-room frame house at Riegal tower, Brunswick County; completed January 19, 1939 by Camp P-73
November 2005: Staffing was discontinued on this tower.

evidence.supports: Entry header names the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: Riegel is listed in Brunswick County

notes_for_editor: The whole history rests on one page, the Forest Lookouts transcription of 1938-40 state report entries. The TN Landforms list only places the tower in Brunswick County. No current-condition, access or photo source was found. A digitalNC catalogue snippet (lib.digitalnc.org record 18726) gives a 125-foot height and a winter 1938-39 build; those pages returned no text to the cache, so they are not cited. The height uses the 120-foot figure from the page. The record's status and access are left as unknown. Entry spells the name Riegal in the report quote; the record uses Riegel.
